Competition among incompatible representations, responses, or rules.
Coordination among differentiated cognitive domains so information in one domain constrains others.
Availability of content to multiple cognitive systems for reasoning, memory, report, or action.
Processing restricted to a subsystem without broad availability to the wider cognitive architecture.
A representational token whose interpretation depends on a rule, convention, or learned relation.
A concrete occurrence of a symbol, word, feature, or code element.
A vocabulary unit grouping inflected or surface forms under a shared lexical identity.
A language unit used in composition according to lexical and grammatical conventions.
A structured linguistic expression composed under syntactic and semantic rules.
A sequence of utterances or texts whose interpretation depends on relations across sentences and context.
An ordered representation of events, agents, causes, and meanings across time.
Identity organization maintained partly through autobiographical narrative and self-interpretation.
A linguistic or logical operation expressing denial or complement of a proposition under a declared semantics.
A construction relating antecedent conditions to consequent claims or actions.
A linguistic act requesting information or resolving uncertainty under conversational norms.
A linguistic construction used to direct, request, or command action.
A meaning construction that maps structure from one domain to another without asserting literal identity.
An utterance whose intended interpretation differs systematically from its literal surface content under context.
Study or representation of how context, goals, speaker relations, and conventions affect meaning in use.
An action performed through language, such as asserting, requesting, promising, or questioning.
A representation of current conversational context, commitments, goals, and unresolved references.
Information or commitments treated as mutually available among conversational participants.
Cognitive processing of other agents, social relations, norms, intentions, and interaction.
The maintained distinction between states attributed to self and states attributed to another agent.
Capacity to represent or infer mental states of other agents while distinguishing them from one own states.
Representing a situation from another agent informational or spatial perspective.
An attachment relation specifically involving another social agent.
Trust concerning another agent expected reliability, intentions, or cooperation.
A specification of how a construct is measured, manipulated, computed, or identified in a particular study or implementation.
A theoretical variable or property that requires operational indicators for empirical use.
A procedure or mapping assigning values to states, events, or reports under declared assumptions.
An observable used as an indirect indicator of a construct; proxy validity must be tested rather than assumed.
Difference between measured value and target quantity arising from noise, bias, resolution, or model mismatch.
Stability or consistency of a measurement under repeated or equivalent conditions.
Degree to which a measure supports the interpretation claimed for it.
An experimentally controlled change to a variable or condition.
A change deliberately imposed on a system to test causal or dynamical consequences.
An experiment that perturbs part of a system and measures resulting changes to infer organization or causal dependence.
Removal, disabling, or isolation of a component or causal path to test its functional contribution.
A comparison condition designed to isolate the effect of a target manipulation.
A condition expected not to produce the target effect and used to detect confounds or spurious inference.
A condition expected to produce a known effect and used to verify that a measurement or manipulation can detect it.
A simpler or alternative model representing what should be expected without the target explanatory structure.
A null model predicting outcomes from stimulus features without self-location, valuation, or temporal-path variables.
A null model predicting outcomes from access/global availability variables without the wider relational geometry.
A null model predicting reports or classifications from behavior while ignoring candidate phenomenal organization.
